spans.note: Section 8.4: Levi factors and unipotent radicals of standard parabolics.

generality.prompt: Does the statement assert a Levi factor containing the chosen maximal torus?
generality.verdict: Yes. For a standard parabolic P_I, the Levi subgroup L_I containing T is determined by the roots generated by I.

spans.note: Proposition 16.1.1: F-defined unipotent radical and Levi subgroups of parabolic F-subgroups.

generality.prompt: Does the Levi factor exist over F rather than only after extending scalars?
generality.verdict: Yes. For a parabolic F-subgroup of a connected reductive F-group, Springer proves existence over F and uniqueness up to Ru(P)(F)-conjugacy.

nodes.title: Standard Parabolics Are Classified by Simple Roots

spans.note: Theorems 8.4.3 and 8.4.4: classification of parabolics containing a fixed Borel.

generality.prompt: Is the classification relative to a fixed pair T subset B?
generality.verdict: Yes. Parabolics containing the chosen Borel are indexed by subsets of the associated set of simple roots; arbitrary parabolics are conjugate to these.

generality.prompt: Are automorphisms of root data classified abstractly, with the equivalence to outer automorphisms of split reductive groups?
generality.verdict: Yes. Aut(root datum) = pinned-Aut of the corresponding split reductive group; for based data, Aut equals the diagram automorphism group (= Out).

generality.prompt: Are based root data defined as the structure invariant of (split) reductive groups over arbitrary fields/bases?
generality.verdict: Yes. Based root data classify split connected reductive groups uniquely up to isomorphism, over any base — the celebrated 'existence and uniqueness theorem'.

spans.note: Theorems 8.3.8 and 8.3.11: Bruhat decomposition and big cell.

generality.prompt: Is the decomposition stated for a connected reductive group with a chosen Borel and maximal torus?
generality.verdict: Yes. The cells are indexed by the Weyl group N_G(T)/T after choosing B containing T.

nodes.title: Bruhat Order Gives Schubert Closure Relations

spans.note: Theorem 8.5.4: closure relations for Bruhat cells.

generality.prompt: Does the closure relation use the Coxeter Bruhat order on W?
generality.verdict: Yes. Schubert variety containment is equivalent to the Bruhat order relation.

generality.prompt: Are Cartan matrices and Dynkin diagrams treated abstractly as combinatorial data classifying root systems?
generality.verdict: Yes. Both are intrinsic to a root system and a choice of base; the diagrammatic classification (A, B, C, D, E_6, E_7, E_8, F_4, G_2) is type-independent.

generality.prompt: Is the duality between the centre of G and the algebraic fundamental group of ĝ G treated as a precise identity (not just a parallel)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The identification Z(ĝ G) = Pontryagin-dual of π_1(G) is an explicit theorem (Kottwitz), proven via root-datum duality.

generality.prompt: Is the behaviour of central isogenies under root-datum duality treated explicitly, including the reversal of direction?
generality.verdict: Yes. A central isogeny G → G' dualises to a central isogeny ĝ G' → ĝ G; the kernels are Pontryagin-dual finite groups.

spans.note: Theorem 10.1.1: existence of a connected reductive group with a prescribed root datum.

generality.prompt: Is this the existence half of the classification by root data?
generality.verdict: Yes. Every abstract root datum occurs as the root datum of a connected reductive algebraic group.

nodes.title: Chevalley Group Construction from a Root Datum

spans.note: Chevalley group construction; Springer follows the original Chevalley 1955 method via Lie algebras.
Demazure's SGA3 construction of the group scheme associated to a based root datum over Z.
Split reductive groups and Chevalley group schemes over Z.

generality.prompt: Is the construction given over Z (Chevalley-Demazure integral form), not just over an algebraically closed field?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction produces a group scheme G over Z (a Chevalley group scheme), and base change G_R = G x_Z R recovers a split reductive group over any base ring R.

spans.note: Theorem 9.6.2: isomorphism theorem for connected reductive groups with isomorphic root data.

generality.prompt: Is this the uniqueness half of the classification of connected reductive groups by root datum?
generality.verdict: Yes. It asserts that an isomorphism of root data is induced by an isomorphism of reductive groups after fixing compatible maximal tori and root subgroup data.

generality.prompt: Is the classification stated uniformly over any base, including the SGA3 / Chevalley-over-Z version?
generality.verdict: Yes. Demazure-Grothendieck classify split reductive groups over any base scheme by their based root datum, with a canonical Z-form (Chevalley group scheme) for each datum.

generality.prompt: Are Coxeter systems and Bruhat order treated abstractly for any Coxeter group, both finite and infinite (affine, hyperbolic)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The definition of a Coxeter system (W, S) and the Bruhat order ≤ is purely combinatorial; the finite case includes Weyl groups, but the framework covers affine and hyperbolic Coxeter groups uniformly.

generality.prompt: Is the dual group construction functorial across the entire family of reductive groups, with the Galois twist for non-split forms?
generality.verdict: Yes. The dual group ĝ G is functorially attached to (G, T) via root-datum duality; the Galois action upgrades it to the L-group for non-split G.

generality.prompt: Is the dual operation on root data treated as an involution at the level of combinatorial data, not just for split reductive groups?
generality.verdict: Yes. Root datum duality is an involution at the level of quadruples (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨) ↦ (X^∨, Φ^∨, X, Φ); it categorifies to Langlands duality of reductive groups via the classification.

generality.prompt: Is the duality of root systems treated abstractly (independent of root data refinement)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The dual root system Φ^∨ ⊆ V^* is intrinsic to any root system Φ ⊆ V; the lattice refinement is added later for root data.

nodes.title: Fundamental Group of a Root Datum

generality.prompt: Is this combinatorial fundamental group defined uniformly for any root datum, recovering the algebraic fundamental group of the associated split reductive group?
generality.verdict: Yes. The construction π_1 = X / Z·Φ^∨ depends only on the root datum and recovers the algebraic fundamental group of the split connected reductive group with that root datum.

generality.prompt: Is the Galois action on root data defined for reductive groups over arbitrary fields, capturing both inner and outer twists?
generality.verdict: Yes. The Galois group acts continuously on the root datum of G_bar k via pinned automorphisms; the action determines G up to quasi-split form, and inner forms add a further H^1(k, G_ad)-cocycle.

generality.prompt: Is the L-group defined uniformly for reductive groups over arbitrary fields with Galois action?
generality.verdict: Yes. The L-group L G = hat G semi-direct Galois (or Weil) is defined for any connected reductive G over a field, using the canonical Galois action on the dual root datum.

generality.prompt: Are L-morphisms defined uniformly for any pair of reductive groups, as the natural target of functoriality?
generality.verdict: Yes. An L-morphism between L-groups is a continuous group homomorphism commuting with projection to the Galois group; it covers all functoriality phenomena.

generality.prompt: Is the Langlands dual group treated for reductive groups over arbitrary fields, with Galois action when needed?
generality.verdict: Yes. The dual group hat G is defined intrinsically from the root datum and is a connected reductive group over C; the Galois action is added separately to form the L-group.

generality.prompt: Is the pinned dual group treated as a canonical structure compatible with both the duality and the Galois action?
generality.verdict: Yes. A pinning of ĝ G is the natural target for the Galois action on the based root datum, making the L-group construction canonical.

generality.prompt: Are pinnings defined uniformly for split reductive groups in any characteristic, with the rigidification statement?
generality.verdict: Yes. A pinning consists of a Borel, maximal torus, and root vectors for the simple roots; pinned isomorphisms are unique once based-root-datum isomorphism is fixed.

spans.note: Theorem 16.1.3: Bruhat lemma for G(F) relative to a minimal parabolic F-subgroup.

generality.prompt: Is this a decomposition of the abstract group G(F), not just of the variety G?
generality.verdict: Yes. The double cosets are P(F)-double cosets indexed by the relative Weyl group.

nodes.title: Relative Root Datum of an F-Reductive Group

spans.note: Theorem 15.3.8: the relative roots and coroots form a root datum.

generality.prompt: Does the theorem allow non-reduced relative root systems?
generality.verdict: Yes. The relative root system can be non-reduced; the root datum statement uses Springer's relative roots and coroots.

nodes.title: Relative Weyl Group Is Generated by Relative Reflections

spans.note: Lemmas 15.3.5 and 15.3.7: relative reflections and generation of the relative Weyl group.

generality.prompt: Is the Weyl group the relative group N_G(S)/Z_G(S)?
generality.verdict: Yes. It is the Weyl group relative to a maximal F-split torus.

generality.prompt: Are root data treated abstractly (as combinatorial data) and not specialised to a particular family of groups?
generality.verdict: Yes. Root data are the combinatorial quadruple (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨); the abstract version is independent of any particular reductive group and admits the based refinement separately.

nodes.title: Root Datum of a Reductive Group

spans.note: Theorem 7.4.3: the roots and coroots of a reductive group form a root datum.

generality.prompt: Is the construction attached to a maximal torus of a connected reductive group?
generality.verdict: Yes. The root datum is built from the character and cocharacter lattices of a maximal torus and the root/coroot system of the adjoint action.

nodes.title: Root Subgroups Generate a Reductive Group

generality.prompt: Does the theorem include both the existence of one-dimensional root subgroups and generation?
generality.verdict: Yes. For a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field, root spaces are one-dimensional and integrate to root subgroups; these together with the maximal torus generate the group.

generality.prompt: Are abstract root systems treated independently of any reductive group, with their classification?
generality.verdict: Yes. Abstract root systems are finite subsets of a Euclidean vector space satisfying axioms; their classification by connected Dynkin diagrams is independent of the reductive-group context.

generality.prompt: Are roots, coroots, and root subgroups defined uniformly for arbitrary reductive groups, not just classical types?
generality.verdict: Yes. Each root α of (G, T) gives a unique closed root subgroup U_α isomorphic to G_a; the coroot is the unique 1-parameter subgroup arising from the SL_2-subgroup attached to ±α.

nodes.title: Weyl Group Is Generated by Root Reflections

spans.note: Theorem 7.1.9: Weyl group generated by reflections in roots.
Proposition 8.2.8: simple roots and simple reflections.

generality.prompt: Does this describe the Weyl group attached to a reductive group and maximal torus?
generality.verdict: Yes. It also records the standard Coxeter-system refinement after choosing a Borel subgroup.

generality.prompt: Are Weyl groups treated both abstractly (as Coxeter groups) and concretely (as N_G(T)/T)?
generality.verdict: Yes. The Weyl group is defined uniformly from the root system; the identification with the normaliser-quotient N_G(T)/T in a reductive group is stated as a theorem.
